questions.question_text: Factorise $-9 + 15k^2$ by taking out a negative common factor.

options.why: Did not flip the $k^2$ term; $15k^2 \div -3 = -5k^2$, so it is $-5k^2$ inside.
Took out $+3$; $3(3 - 5k^2) = 9 - 15k^2$, the opposite sign of every term.
Dropped the square; $15k^2 \div -3 = -5k^2$, which keeps the power.
